BIOE 5710 — Experimental Systems and Synthetic Bioengineering | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor.

4 semester hoursGraduateLectureusually offered: fall, springBostonTraditional

Introduces experimental aspects of systems and synthetic bioengineering. Offers students an opportunity to learn how to plan and execute quantitative experiments, how to apply engineering principles to design laboratory research and to interpret data, and how to design and implement synthetic genetic or enzymatic circuits. Through team projects, explores techniques in nucleic acid, protein, and genetic engineering; quantitative measurements at the single-cell level and beyond; design and applications of synthetic circuits; and discusses ethical considerations.
